body: Open audio-language models are used as judges of generated music: given a clip and its text prompt, the model rates the clip, and the judge is validated by how well its ratings correlate with expert ratings. The correlation does not show what the judge responds to: the music, the text prompt, or the way the question is asked. We propose four probes that test each of these, three of them read against a control computed from the human ratings: removing the audio, replacing the clip with another model's clip for the same prompt, swapping the order of two clips in pairwise judging, and rewording the instruction. We apply them to five open judges on all 2,748 clips of MusicEval, and the last two to the SongEval songs. Without audio, no judge exceeds what the prompt alone predicts from the human ratings, and for prompt alignment every judge falls below it. With audio, every judge follows the clip it hears when rating prompt alignment, two do when rating musical quality, and the strongest judge's quality score tracks the experts' alignment rating more than their quality rating. The pairwise verdicts of the four smaller judges follow the position of a clip in the pair (its slot) rather than its quality on both rating sets. For musical quality, rewording the instruction moves the correlation of most judges as much as changing the judge. MusicEval's prompt assignment bounds any prompt-only judge at the model level. We recommend reporting the four probes with every music judge.
summaryZh: 本文探讨了音频语言模型作为音乐生成评估器（Judge）的有效性。研究人员提出了四种探针方法，通过移除音频、替换片段、交换顺序及重写指令等手段，测试模型在评估时是否真正关注音乐内容。实验发现，模型在缺乏音频时表现不佳，且在评估时容易受到指令措辞和片段位置的影响，而非单纯基于音乐质量。研究建议在音乐评估中必须报告这些探针结果，以确保评估的客观性。

aiReview.reasonZh: 该研究通过四种探针方法揭示了音频语言模型在音乐生成评估中的偏见，为评估指标的可靠性提供了重要参考。
